title: Add a benchmark
subtitle: Drop a file or paste a link. Heimdall says what it found, drafts the tasks, proves each check passes the right answer and fails wrong ones, then adds the ready tasks to a private benchmark.

source.description: A spreadsheet (CSV), JSON Lines, tickets, a zip of a benchmark folder, a Hugging Face dataset, a Harbor id such as terminal-bench@2.0, a GitHub repository, an OpenAPI spec or a trace export.
source.drop: Drop a file here or pick one
source.pastePlaceholder:
question,answer
What is the hotel cap per night?,250
source.connectionHint: The id of a secret holding a token, for a gated Hugging Face dataset.
source.cannotDraft: Recognised, but it cannot become tasks here yet
source.nothing: Give a link, a file or pasted rows.

found.samples: First rows (e-mail addresses and phone numbers hidden)
found.estimate: About {{tasks}} tasks and {{runs}} readiness runs. Readiness runs replay fixed answers on a worker with no model, so they cost nothing. Drafting makes no model call.
found.estimateJudge: Rubric grading adds {{judge}} judge calls, paid on your own model key.

plan.suiteHint: A new id creates a private benchmark; an existing one adds tasks to it.
plan.suiteInvalid: Use 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit.
plan.suiteBuiltin: {{id}} is a built-in benchmark and cannot be changed. Pick a new id.
plan.suiteExisting: Adds tasks to your benchmark {{id}} ({{count}} tasks now).
plan.heldOutHint: Held-out tasks stay private: they are never shown in shared results, so a score on them cannot be gamed.
plan.draftHint: Nothing is added to a benchmark until you publish.

preview.description: Each task exactly as the agent sees it, how it is checked, and the controls that prove the check. Accept or reject each task.
preview.problems: Rows that could not become tasks
preview.public: Public data: models may have seen it in training.
preview.empty: No task was drafted. The problems below say why.

ready.description: Each task runs in the real sandbox: the right answer must pass, and the empty answer, wrong answers and gaming attempt must fail. Generated words never decide that a task is ready; these runs do.
ready.confirm: Run the readiness checks on {{count}} tasks? Each task runs its right answer three times and every control once; rubric-graded tasks call the judge on your own key.
ready.problems: File problems found before anything ran

publish.description: Ready, accepted tasks join the benchmark, private to your organization. Held-out tasks get a hidden marker so a leak can be traced.
publish.unready: Also publish accepted tasks that are not ready (they stay out of evaluations until their readiness checks pass on the benchmark)
publish.recheck: {{count}} tasks need the readiness checks on the benchmark before evaluations use them.
